name: Fère-Champenoise
summary: The allied cavalry, marching on Paris, rode down Marmont's and Mortier's corps on the plain, and then Pacthod's and Amey's National Guard divisions, which formed squares and fought on until the Tsar himself rode in to accept their surrender.

toCome.name: Marmont's Corps
toCome.formation: Ricard's, Lagrange's and Arrighi's divisions, with Bordesoulle's and Merlin's cavalry
toCome.summary: Caught on the open plain by the allied cavalry marching on Paris, and driven back with heavy loss; Bordesoulle's horse was routed.

toCome.name: Mortier's Corps
toCome.formation: Christiani's, Curial's and Charpentier's Guard divisions, with Roussel d'Hurbal's and Ghigny's cavalry
toCome.summary: Fell back beside Marmont's under the allied charges; Belliard's horse pushed Pahlen's aside.

toCome.name: Pacthod's National Guards
toCome.summary: About five thousand eight hundred men and sixteen guns, escorting a convoy, who formed squares and fought on until surrounded; Pacthod, Amey and their brigadiers were taken.

toCome.name: The Russian Guard Cavalry
toCome.summary: The Guard cuirassiers and light cavalry, with Depreradovich's 1st Cuirassier Division, which made the decisive charge.

toCome.name: Pahlen's Cavalry
toCome.summary: Some three thousand five hundred horse, with Ilovaisky's Cossacks and Kretov's 2nd Cuirassier Division.

toCome.name: Korff's and Vasilchikov's Cavalry
toCome.summary: The cavalry of Langeron's and Sacken's corps, with Seslavin's Cossacks.

toCome.name: Nostitz's Cuirassiers
toCome.summary: About three thousand seven hundred, with Desfours's brigade.

toCome.name: The Crown Prince of Württemberg's Cavalry
toCome.summary: About two thousand horse of the IV Corps.
